answer: Keep the rubric as the single KICD CBE criterion with all four levels (Exceeds, Meets, Approaches, Below Expectations), using the KICD wording verbatim. The current rubric already follows the specified KICD descriptors, but the 'Approaches' descriptor needs to be checked against the KICD text, and the four levels must stay visible to teachers and learners. Since the partner contract has only three level fields, the Below Expectations level is carried in the existing belowExpectations field (it is in the rubric already). No further wording change is needed unless the partner schema is extended. Teachers can approve the rubric as is.
alternative: Merge Approaches and Below Expectations into one 'Developing' field to fit three levels, but this departs from the KICD four-level rubric and is not recommended.

answer: Keep the 16-minute written assessment in class, but state clearly that it is a short-form check and that Q4 and Q5 may be finished as a take-home task if time runs out. A full five-question paper in 16 minutes is tight for many learners, so a safety valve is more realistic than the current wording. All five questions and benchmarks stay the same.

edits.old: Learners work in silence. They may use the completed Toolkit poster on the wall.
edits.new: Learners work in silence. They may use the completed Toolkit poster on the wall. If a learner has not finished Q4 and Q5 when time is called, they complete them as a take-home task and return them next period; Q1-Q3 are marked in class.

alternative: Move Q4 and Q5 to a separate next-period task for all learners and keep only Q1-Q3 in the 16 minutes.

answer: Confirm the current split. Keep the 3-minute regular heptagon task (KICD outcome e) and Heron's formula (KICD outcome c) in class, with the object search and shoelace extension as take-home work. This keeps all KICD outcomes taught in class and fits the 40 minutes. No wording change is needed.
alternative: Move the heptagon task to the start of Lesson 6 as a retrieval warm-up, which frees Lesson 5 time for more tile-costing practice.
